title: Rambo: First Blood Part II
build: Ocean's original disk, mastered 4 December 1985 ("MASTER DATE 04/12/85 NO:014.006.2" on track 18, sector 2), protected by the XROM system of Tequila Sunrise, Belgium; a G64 image

records.c: Bytes left in zero page by the loader's stack-overwrite stage; the game's own start-up (game_init at $1695) clears $02-$FF, so nothing of the game runs or reads them here.
Remains of the loader's $0100 stub (copies the $FF00 page to $0200, sets $01 to $E7 and returns); a loader leftover that the game never calls.

Starts a game: game_init ($1695), restores the map ($09CC), plays tune $0C, enables all sprites, then the main loop at $0393: frame wait, scroll redraw, coarse scroll, stick-driven direction, items, enemies, the hut-door test, panel weapons, music tick, collisions, score draw and add, firing, enemy bullets, projectiles, enemy spawns, energy, the end-of-task test and the sort, every pass.
An address named only by the BIT $03A0 skip in the music driver at $83D3 (no code reads it); the main loop continues here.
Plays tune 4 once when the map row $FE/$FF enters rows $88-$EF of the first 256 ; $040B remembers it has been started and is cleared when the row leaves the band.
Set while the map row is in the band where music_zone_check ($03EA) has started tune 4.
Adds A to score digit X ($248F,x), from the jump table at $037C.
Clears the six score digits ($2483) and the six pending additions ($248F).
If $0F (the end-of-life or end-of-task flag) is set, falls into the task-end screen; otherwise returns.
Shows message screen 3 via $044D, decrements $0F and restarts the game at game_start.
Sets $0F and shows the message whose number is in A, then falls into $0430, which shows message 3.

Picks the next mission message: with $0AFF clear it shows message A; otherwise message A plus $08EB (whether the hut rescue has begun), or message 3 with $0F set to 3 when $E6 is set and the rescue has not begun.

Shows a full-screen mission message: blanks sprites, stops sound (command 1), saves zero page $E0-$FF, prints the screen layout with the text printer ($C000, inline script $106A), swaps in the front-end graphics ($C003), selects tune and text by A from tables $0565 (tune) and $056F (text pointer), waits until the tune ends (driver command 2 returns zero while a tune plays), restores zero page, and either resumes the jungle ($04F2) or returns to the caller's caller when $0F is set.
The inline script address after the JSR $C000 at $0474: the six-byte script at $106A.
message_screen continues after the frame script: swaps the font in, picks the message's tune and text.
The inline script address after the JSR $C000 at $049A; message_screen writes it from the message table $056F before printing.
The high byte of the message script address at $049D.
message_screen continues: waits each frame on raster $C8, plays music, and polls driver command 2 until the tune ends; then restores the screen, the font, the sprites and the music.
The inline script address after the JSR $C000 at $04D6: the closing script ($055F).
message_screen continues after the closing script: restores zero page and returns or resumes.

After a message, re-enters the map: X = $0537 selects a restart position from tables $0538 (row lo), $053A (row hi), $053C (column), then scrolls $28 times to rebuild the screen, sets the screen registers and returns; with $0537 = 0 it sets $0F to 1 and unwinds the stack to end the game.
The restart position message_screen saves (A of $044D): 0 ends the game, 1 and 2 pick a position from the tables below.
Low bytes of the map row for restart positions 1 and 2.
High bytes of the map row for restart positions 1 and 2.
Map columns for restart positions 1 and 2.
Counts the 40 scroll steps resume_after_message uses to redraw the screen.
The 32 bytes of zero page $E0-$FF that message_screen saves while the front end's printer uses them, and puts back after.
Printer script printed by message_screen as it closes (inline at $04D6).
The tune command for each message, at the even bytes (message_screen indexes it by twice the message number): $0B, $06, $07, $0B, $0A.
Addresses of the five messages' printer scripts: $0579, $05D5, $0651, $06C5, $06D9.
The message script table continues.

The mission messages as printer scripts: TASK ONE COMPLETED. YOUR DATA REVEALS AMERICAN P.O.W.S TO BE RESCUED; NOW RESCUE THE P.O.W.S FROM THE CAMP. USE ANY ENEMY EQUIPMENT NECESSARY; YOUR PRESENCE HAS BEEN RELAYED TO ENEMY H.Q. A GUNSHIP IS NOW ON COURSE AND IN PURSUIT; GAME OVER; CONGRATULATIONS. THANKS TO YOU TEN P.O.W.S HAVE BEEN RETURNED TO THE HOMELAND; and YOU KNOW YOU MUST NOW RETURN TO GET MORE UNFORTUNATE SOLDIERS TRAPPED BY ENEMY FORCES. $5B is a space and $FF starts a printer command.
Named only by the BIT $05A0 skip in the music driver ($84B2); message 0's script continues here (YOUR DATA REVEALS ...), up to $05D4.
Named only by the BIT $06A0 skip in the music driver ($83C1); message 2's script continues here (it runs from $0651 to $06C4).
Named only by the BIT $07A0 skip in the music driver ($83D0); the last message script ends here.
Locks the stick (input_locked at $1CE4 = 1), so read_stick returns nothing; reached through the jump table at $0370.
Unlocks the stick ($1CE4 = 0); reached through the jump table at $0373.
Waits for the next frame: the interrupt's flag at $2334 (frame_wait_irq at $1D66), then copies object state for the multiplexer ($1D33), then waits for the second interrupt flag at $22C4 ($2112).
Returns in A the two score digits at $2483,x*2 packed as a BCD byte (high digit in the top nibble); used to copy the score into the heroes table.
Moves the freed POWs: for each of four slots ($0847,x) calls pow_walk ($084B) or pow_spawn ($0803); when all are out ($0846 = 0) and none walks, clears the rescue flags $093F, $0940 and $0B00.
Counts down the POW slots handled this frame; negative when none is still walking.

Starts one POW leaving the hut: on a 1-in-50 chance, while POWs remain ($0846), places object X at the hut ($0941/$0942), sprite $CF, colour 12, sets a walk count of 20 in $0847,x and the score award 2.
POWs still to leave the hut (ten at the start of the rescue).
Each walking POW's step count: 20 down to 2 while it walks south, 1 while it walks east until its X reaches $AA, 0 when the slot is free.
Walks a freed POW: state 1 moves it right (X to $AA) with frames $D3-$D6, otherwise it walks down $0847,x steps with frames $CF-$D2; the frame advances every third call (pow_anim_tick at $0897).
Animation divider per POW: counts $08A8,x down from 2 and returns carry set on the frame the animation should advance.
Animation dividers of the four POWs.

While the rescue runs ($093F), moves the hut position with the vertical scroll and forces the stick variables: to "down" while $093F is above 1, so the screen scrolls, and to nothing once it reaches 1; then runs pow_run_update.

When Rambo stands on the hut-door character ($15F8 = $E0) with weapon 0 selected and the rescue has not started ($08EB), starts it: sets $093F to $28, records the hut's map position, frees ten POWs ($0846), replaces the hut tile ($1340), plays sound $1B and clears the objects (object_reset at $0A8B).
Set once the hut has been opened; picks the later messages.
hut_door_check continues: the rescue can start only once the item for it has been taken ($0B00) and none is running ($093F).
The rescue sequence's state: $28 counted down to 1 while the screen scrolls, then held at 1 until every POW is out, then cleared.
Set while the POWs come out; pauses the enemies and the marker scans.
Screen row of the opened hut's door, where POWs appear.
Screen column of the opened hut's door.
Clears the five enemy slots ($11E5, $45) and the seven slots of $1919/$4A: the four enemy bullets and Rambo's three shots.
The stick reading stick_changed compares against.
The stick reading just taken by stick_changed.

Shows the opening briefing: swaps in the front-end graphics, plays tune 9, prints the briefing text (inline script $1056), waits on raster $64 each frame until the stick is pushed, then shows the second page (script $106A) and swaps back.
The inline script address after the JSR $C000 at $0980: the briefing's first page ($1056).
mission_briefing continues after its first page: waits for the stick or the end of the tune.
Named only by the BIT $09A0 skips in the driver's three voice copies ($8869, $8BA5, $8EDC); mission_briefing continues here, leaving its wait loop.
Reads the stick; returns Z clear and A = fire bit when the reading differs from the last one in $095A.
Named only by a BIT $09A9 skip in the tune data's native code ($9C36); stick_changed continues here.
The inline script address after the JSR $C000 at $09C2: the six-byte script at $106A, which prints no text.
mission_briefing ends: swaps the game's font back.
Copies the clean map ($E770-$EEDF) over the working map ($E000-$E76F), undoing every tile the last game destroyed.
The source page in the LDA $E770,y at $09DA, stepped by map_restore.
The destination page in the STA $E000,y at $09DD, stepped by map_restore.
Tests key code $3F (RUN/STOP) with key_test ($2631) and toggles $0A19 on each new press; the interrupt stops the game while $0A19 is set.
Set while RUN/STOP is held, so one press toggles once.
Set while the game is paused; the interrupt then freezes play and silences the SID.

Tests Rambo (object 13) against the item in object 12 with a 12-by-10 box (box_hit at $2496). A weapon item ($0BC3,x >= 0) adds its bit to $19ED, updates the panel and scores 3; taking slot 3 ends the jungle stage ($0AB2); an item with bit 7 set counts into $0AFF and scores 5.
Clears the enemy, bullet and item state: positions to $0A, the active and timer arrays to zero.

Item slot 3 taken: resets the objects, shows message 0 ($0435), runs the helicopter stage ($3003) with $08EB, and on return places Rambo at the column and row the helicopter stage left in X and Y and redraws the screen.
Counts the items with bit 7 taken (item_pickup_check); once non-zero enemies spawn without a budget and the messages change.
Set when Rambo comes back from the helicopter stage (item3_taken at $0AC6) and cleared when the POWs are out (pow_run_update); hut_door_check needs it.

Places the item sprite (object 12) for the first of the four map items ($0BB7 column, $0BBB/$0BBF row) that is within the visible window, converting its map position to screen coordinates; slot 3 sets up a second sprite (object 4) beside it.
Named only by the BIT $0BA0 skips in the music driver at $83C4 and $84AF; item_place continues here (no item on screen: clears $CF and hides object 12).
Named only by the BIT $0BA9 skip in the tune data's native code ($9C33); item_place continues: hides object 4 unless it is in use ($11E9).
The item slot item_place found on screen.
Map column of each of the four items.
Map column of item 3 (the helicopter), which item3_taken and game_init rewrite.

Low byte of item 3's map row.
High byte of the map row of each item.
High byte of item 3's map row.

The values item_kind starts each game with (slots 0-2; game_init copies them).
Sprite frame of each item.
One enemy per frame, round robin over slots 0-3: if it is walking (state 1), tests it against Rambo (enemy_touch at $0BE6).
Round-robin slot for enemy_hit_check.
Box test of enemy X against Rambo (12 by 10); on a hit adds 4 to the damage counter $0B and kills the enemy (enemy_kill at $15A0).
One bullet per frame, round robin over slots 0-3: tests an active bullet against Rambo (bullet_touch at $0C33).
Box test of bullet X against Rambo; on a hit adds 7 to the damage counter $0B, plays sound $18 and removes the bullet ($24FD).
Round-robin slot for bullet_hit_check.
Draws the full energy bar from the template at $4840/$4855 into the panel at $4400/$4440 and sets the energy to $30.
Takes one unit of damage a frame from $0B: decrements the energy $0CC3, clears the matching pixels of the bar (masks at $0CC4), and sets $0F to 1 when the energy runs out.
Rambo's energy, $30 when full; each unit is one step of the panel bar.
The eight bit masks energy_tick uses to clear the bar a pixel at a time.

Tests the S key (code $0D); on each new press toggles sound effects ($0D11) and switches which voices the music may use between 7 (all, music on) and 0 (none, music off) through command $1A, value in $0CF9.
Set while S is held.
The voices the music may use, 7 or 0, which music_toggle_key alternates and sends with command $1A.
Plays sound effect A through the driver ($8100) unless effects are switched off ($0D11), keeping X and Y.
Set when the S key has switched sound effects off.
The effect play_effect was asked for.

After a coarse scroll ($1D30 set by the scroll code), draws the newly exposed edge: bit 0 the top row ($279E), bit 1 the bottom row ($2769), bit 2 the left column ($26B1), bit 3 the right column ($2681).
Animates an enemy in state 5 (rising): counts $0D5E,x down, nudging it up by the table at $0D60; when done gives it a random type ($120B) and makes it walk.
Frames each rising enemy has left (state 5).
Row steps of the rising animation, read from the end of rise_count.
Scans eight characters a frame of the visible screen ($32/$33 walk through rows $402C onward) for character $93; for each, may start an enemy rising there (hole_spawn at $0DB7).

On a 1-in-4 chance, if that enemy slot is free, starts an enemy rising from the hole just found: state 5, colour 9, frame $76 (type $0B) when the character below is $67, else frame $78 (type $0C), position from the scan row and column.
Character index within the row hole_scan has reached.
Row counter for hole_scan (17 rows).
While no rescue runs, looks along screen row $42D0 for the marker character $FD, eight cells a frame; when found places object 4 there with state 2 and colour $0B.
Position of marker_scan along its row; negative when finished.
Each frame clears one byte of the sprite data at $7ED8-$7EDF and sets a bit from $19EF in another, walking two indices round the eight bytes: an animated pattern in that sprite.
Index into $19EF for sprite_bit_cycle.
Byte index into $7ED8 for sprite_bit_cycle.
Called by the column drawer when it meets marker tile $FD: places object 4 at the left or right edge, row from X.
Called by the row drawer when it meets marker tile $FD: places object 4 at the top edge, column from $267E.
Updates the five enemy slots: moves the active ones (enemy_step at $0F68), may spawn new ones in free slots ($118B), and on a 1-in-200 chance adds one to the spawn budget $119B.

Moves enemy X by its state: 5 rising, 4 dying (advances the frame every 4 calls, removes it at frame $82), 2 and 3 the object-4 sequence (2 waits for $0FF6, 3 moves it by $0FEA for $0FF5 frames, then kills it), otherwise walking: picks a direction ($100A), checks the ground, animates and moves.

Step sizes added to object 4's Y in state 3, indexed by its timer $0FF5 divided by 4.

Counts destroyed tiles of kind $30; object 4 leaves state 2 when it is non-zero.
The walking enemy's frame: steers ($100A), keeps it inside the window ($115E), sometimes picks a new direction (random under 10, $1039), then animates ($1070).
Reads the character under enemy X ($1601); characters $1B-$29 are open ground and let it move; anything else counts $1046,x up and after 10 frames removes the enemy.
Gives enemy X a random walking type from the eight in $120B.

Colour byte in the message frame script, set before printing.

Advances enemy X's walk animation: waits $10DA,x frames (2, or 20 in state 2), then steps through the frame list at $10BC from the start $10B1 gives for its type $11EA,x, a zero ending the list; sets the sprite pointer $8B,x.
Start of each enemy type's frame list in $10BC.

Moves enemy X by its type's step ($113F X step, $114C Y step) plus the scroll deltas $0C and $0D; a blocked enemy ($1046,x) moves only with the scroll. X is nine bits ($7D,x and bit 0 of $61,x).

Calls the music driver's play routine (command 0 of $8100), once a pass of the main loop.
Removes enemy X ($116B: state 0, position $0A, one fewer active) when it leaves rows $0A-$C4 or columns 2-$A8 (half-pixel units); otherwise moves it ($10DF).

For a free slot other than 4, while the spawn budget $119B lasts (or always once $0AFF is set), places a new enemy at a random point of one of seven entry zones ($11EF/$11F6 X base and range, $11FD/$1204 Y base and range) with the zone's type ($120B) and a random colour from $11E1.
How many enemies may still be spawned; explosions and shots add to it, a 1-in-200 chance a frame adds one.

Animates Rambo: when the stick direction ($1D06 low nibble) changes, restarts the walk cycle from $12CD for that direction; otherwise every fourth call steps through the frame list $12D8, setting the sprite pointer $D1 and $98 (frame plus 4).

Replaces the map tile under a point ($18E9 Y, $18EA/$18EB X) by its damaged form from table $1241 in the working map at $E000 (tile $30 also counts $0FF6), then redraws the part of that tile's 8-by-8 characters that is on screen at $4000.

One of Rambo's three shots a frame: for a shot of type 5 or 8 (the explosive ones), checks the character under it; off open ground ($1B-$29) it explodes there ($189C).

One of Rambo's three shots a frame (round robin over $1528): for an active shot that is not type 9, tests it against the four enemies (shot_hit at $1539).

Tests shot X (type in A) against enemies 3 to 0 with a box from tables $1529/$1531 by type; on a hit, explosive types 5 and 8 explode ($18EC), type $0A passes through, others end ($17EF); the enemy dies ($15A0): frame $7E, state 4, colour 1, award 1 to score digit $2492 and sound $12.

Reads the four characters around Rambo's feet (offsets $15F9) and clears the matching stick bits ($15FD masks) for any that is not open ground ($1B-$29), so he cannot walk into scenery; keeps the last character read in $15F8.

As $1601 for a shot, whose X is eight bits in two-pixel units.

Sets up a new game: clears zero page, sorts the object list, installs the game interrupt ($211B), clears enemies, places the four items, sets energy, scroll, weapons owned (7: the first three), video bank 1 (screen $4000, characters $7800), colours and sprite modes, shows the briefing ($095C), draws the first screen by scrolling 25 rows, and draws the panel.
